22. I have heard the learned Advocate of both the parties at length and perused the record of the case.

23. It appears that one Abdul Khaleque along with his daughter Amina Khaleque instituted Title Suit No. 181 of 1994 on 24-6-1994 and on the same day he has obtained an order of temporary injunction. But it appears from the statement of the plaint to the effect that "the plaintiff No. 1 while owing and possessing the balance 25 and 3/4 decimals of land in the northern portion of the plot No. 158,4 decimals of land was shown acquired in LA Case No. 40- A/89-90 as stated hereinabove but no notice of requisition was served upon the plaintiff No. 1. In the said state of things Rajuk and the DC Dhaka, the LA Authority all on a sudden came to the plaintiff No. 1's SP Plot No. 49 i.e. north western portion of CS Plot No. 158 with bull-dozers and demolished the semi-pucca tin sheds of the plaintiffs No. 1 and forcibly took possession of about 17 and 1/4 decimals of land out of 25 and 3/4 decimals of land of the plaintiff No. 1 and around 9 decimals of land of the plaintiff No. 2's 10 decimals and over the said land the scheme of the link road in between Green Road and Mirpur Road (pantha Path West) was materialized."

24. Which shows that possession of the land has already been taken by the acquiring authority before institution of their suit, which has been filed on 28-6-1994 and, as such; it appears that the possession of the property taken before institution of the suit the question of mandatory injunction does not arise at all. However, the plaintiff ought to have filed a case under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act or an application under section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure for recovery of possession.

25. It further appears that from the schedule of plaint it appears that plaintiff No. 1 and 2 claimed total 48 decimals of land out of 5.68 acres of land but there is no assertion as to which portion of the said big plot the plaintiff obtained 48 decimals of land. The plaintiff filed a suit for declaration as well as permanent injunction but in a suit declaration or suit for permanent injunction the plaintiff is to show his exclusive possession by determining the boundary in which portion he is in exclusive possession of the suit property but in the instant case the plaintiff failed to show the boundary. It has been held in the case of Abdul Quddus Matabbar vs Yousuf Ali Bayati reported in 17 BLT (AD) 45, that in a simple suit for declaration of titIe in respect of 10.47 acres of land out of 13.14 acres of land is not maintainable as from the evidence of PWs it is clear that the suit land is ejmali property and without a prayer for partition the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. In the instant case total claim of the plaintiff is 48 decimals of land out of 5.68 decimals of land from the plaint it is clear that except 48 decimals of land and rest properties owned by other persons and they were not made party in the instant suit nor has partition been claimed in the instant suit. Nor there was any specific assertion as to which portion of the said land the plaintiff is in possession. Rather from the schedule it appears that the schedule as mentioned is vogue unspecific thus violated the mandatory perversion under Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, runs thus:-

"Where the subject-matter of the suit is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description of the property sufficient to identity it, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement of survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers."

26. In the instant case the plaintiff mentioned the boundaries of 5.68 decimals of land not the land of his own 48 decimals as he claim, thus the mandatory provision of law has not been complied with and as such the suit itself is not maintainable.

27. In the instant case, the plaintiff filed a suit for permanent injunction. But from the judgment of the trial Court as well as from the judgment of the appellate Court shows that both the Courts below did not record any finding that the plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the specific portion of the land and separate share of the suit plot well demarcated by boundaries so as to entitle the plaintiffs to retain their possession against their co-shares till partition by metes and bounds. The similar view was taken in the case of Abdus Samad Akand vs Abdul Halim Maji reported in 50 DLR (AD) 6.

28. Under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, in the joint property, part of the said property, cannot be declared in their favour without the partition. Similar view was taken in the case of Amiruddin Mondal Md Ashraf Ali reported in 11 BLC 134.

29. The principle of law is that the plaintiff is to prove his case, for the weakness of the defendants the plaintiffs is not entitled to a decree, said principle has been settled in various decisions of our sub- continent. The case of Shahana Bibi vs Nur Islam reported in 4 BLC 195, the case of Md Abdur Rahim vs Sree Sree Gredhari Jeo reported in 27 DLR 72, the case of ADC (Revenue), Pabna vs Md Abdul Halim Mia, 48 DLR (AD) 141 (approved the decision of27 DLR 227, the case of Ram Chandra Arya vs Man Singh reported in AIR 1968 (SC) 954, the case of Province of East Pakistan vs Haji Muslimullah reported in 20 DLR 262, the case of Walivs Manish Ali reported in 17 DLR (SC) 536, the case of Master Abdul Aziz vs Abani Mohan Mukherjee reported in 30 DLR (SC) 221, the case of Shefar Alam Nizamee vs Mrs Karisma Begum Haridunnessa reported in 40 DLR 422, the case of Alauddin Munshi vs Mainuddin Talukder reported in 14 DLR 724 and the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property, Chandpur reported in 39 DLR (AD) 223.

30.. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No.1 (Tha) raised a point that the judgment of both the below are concurrent and, as such, concurrent finding of facts by the Courts below cannot disturbed at the revisional stage. But as I find from the judgment that the finding of facts of both the Courts below are not concurrent for which the appellate Court dismissed the Title Appeal No. 46 of 1997 and allowed Title Appeal No. 54 of 1997.

<u>31. Furthermore mere concurrent finding of facts does not give any authority not to interfere in the judgment but in a revisional jurisdiction it can be interfered if there is error of law. Mere error of law is not enough until and unless it causes failure of justice.</u>

32. In the instant case, I find that there are various error of law in disposing of the suit (non-complying Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure) which is a mandatory provision. Order III, rule 1 and 2, CPC, section 42 of the specific Relief Act, section 120 of the Evidence Act.

33. It has been held in the case of Abdur Rahim vs Arifur Rahman reported in 50 DLR 166, that: -

"A Court of revision under section 115(1) CPC can interfere with the findings of fact, as the final Court of facts, only in exceptional circumstances when the finding are shockingly perverse of these are vitiated by non-reading and misreading of the material evidence or misconstruction of any important document affecting the merit of the suit."

34. In the instant case as it appears from the plaint that the defendant No. 1-4 has already taken possession or the suit property thereafter they filed the suit, on 26-4-1994, which they have admitted in their plaint in paragraph No. 12. Since the defendants already taken possession a suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable. The plaintiff is to pray for recovery of possession. Furthermore, description of the schedule property as mentioned in the schedule is not specific. Though the plaintiff filed another suit for demarcation of the suit property as it appears from the record. The said suit being Demarcation Suit No .31 of 1994, which was ended on dismissal. Against which an appeal was preferred by the plaintiff but the said appeal was not persuaded.

35. From the facts and circumstances of the case as discussed above, I find substance in the instant Rule. The plaintiffs instituted the suit without determining his claim. However, they may file a suit partition if they so advised.

36. Accordingly, both the Rules are made absolute however, without any Order as to costs.

38. The suit is hereby dismissed.
